title: Chapter 26: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

blocks.content: PFRDA was established to promote old age income security by establishing, developing and regulating pension funds.

rows: No tax benefits (except for Govt employees under 3-yr lock-in)

items: PFRDA became a statutory body under the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 2013, which took effect in February 2014.
NPS is mandatory for all Central Government employees joining service on or after January 1, 2004, excluding the Armed Forces.
Atal Pension Yojana (APY) specifically targets the unorganised sector and is regulated through the PFRDA architecture.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: PFRDA is the statutory regulatory body responsible for the supervision and regulation of pensions in India.
Initially constituted by a Government resolution in December 2003, it attained full statutory status under the PFRDA Act, 2013.
The authority comprises a Chairperson and up to six members appointed by the Central Government, with at least three being whole-time members.
It administers major pension schemes including the National Pension System (NPS) and the Atal Pension Yojana (APY).
